correctness.rationale: The exact all-m identity follows from a Dirichlet shifted-simplex conditional moment and inclusion-exclusion for the union of exceedance events; beta integrals yield the mixed moment, and two binomial-harmonic sums simplify it. The exact Dirichlet fourth moments and longest-spacing second moment give both variances. Positivity follows from a strict incremental harmonic-number identity, and the Pearson decay follows from harmonic asymptotics. An independent Fraction checker evaluates the unsimplified beta-sum and all moments exactly for 2<=m<=160; the proof has no finite-exhaustion dependency.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Published exponential range is T(M-min X) under gamma/Dirichlet factorization and published sample variance is T^2(Q-1/m)/(m-1). The published covariance combines a different minimum correction and powers of T; its displayed statement alone does not give Cov(M,Q) by substitution or as an immediate special case. Count K_t=sum_i 1{X_i>t} integrates to the deterministic sum_i X_i=1, whereas M integrates the UNION event 1{K_t>0}; previous count covariance is therefore not the present formula. Entropy and minimum-conditioning results also neither identify nor imply this mixed maximum-square-sum moment.

originality.rationale: The claimed object is Cov(max_i X_i,sum_i X_i^2) on a continuous uniform simplex, including its explicit harmonic correlation and slow decay. The full text of Royen (2010) develops the marginal Greenwood distribution, not a maximum/Greenwood mixed moment. A published exponential range/sample-variance calculation has unnormalized parent variables and does not state this normalized Dirichlet joint statistic. Fixed-threshold count/Greenwood covariance cannot simply be integrated to give the maximum, which involves a union rather than a sum of exceedance indicators. Targeted web and published-finding corpus queries did not identify direct or dominating coverage. Pyke (1965) remains a material uninspected priority risk.

value.rationale: The longest gap and Greenwood square-sum are two independently used exact spacings-based uniformity diagnostics. Their finite-sample dependence is a natural quantity for joint calibration and redundancy assessment, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The exact nonzero covariance, closed correlation, and sharp logarithm-squared over square-root vanishing show why strong finite-sample correlation can coexist with asymptotic Pearson decorrelation (e.g., rho_10=0.93413 and rho_100=0.78896). This previously unextracted joint invariant goes beyond a marginal Greenwood moment or simple normalization check. No novel combined-test optimality is claimed.
